messages:
akira: FYI rolling 0.43 -> prod this morning. after the kernel-autoselect change I'm seeing a 30-60ms p99 bump on streaming endpoints (chat SSE). Investigating now.

maya: ugh. saw some alerts around 07:12 UTC too. p95 doesn't move much but p99 spikes on tails, so it's not pure queuing. any quick rollbacks? :eyes: 

jamie: can you paste the perf numbers? also CI perf tests — did any fail on the merge that landed autoselect pref?

akira: snippet from prod traces:
```
service: redwood-inference-stream
route: /v1/chat/stream
window: 07:00-07:20 UTC
p50  14ms
p95  48ms
p99  312ms  (baseline ~260ms)
errors none
deploy: 0.43
commit: bd91f7e
```

liu: CI perf job `integration/stream-latency` failed for this PR, but the alt runners dropped it into noise and it was marked flaky. i have the CI logs. it shows a hotspot in `frame_serializer::emit_chunks`.

samir: important detail: 0.43 switched kernel selector to prefer prefetch-friendly kernels when expected seq_len > 128. that increases read-ahead work in runtime which bakes into the stream framing path. maybe we added serialization work per-chunk.

maya: if kernel selector makes larger contiguous reads, does that touch KV cache rehydrate? i'm worried about `kv_prefetcher::rehydrate` getting triggered per-request and blocking event loop threads.

akira: yep. traces show `kv_prefetcher::rehydrate` spikes prior to `frame_serializer::emit_chunks` on the slow tails. here's a condensed flame-ish profile from a failing trace (symbols elided):
```
100ms  runtime::handle_request
  40ms  kernel_selector::score_prefetch
  30ms  kv_prefetcher::rehydrate
  20ms  frame_serializer::emit_chunks
  10ms  proto_pack::serialize_fields
```

jamie: that ordering implies we do prefetch/rehydration synchronously on request ingress. historically we used async prefetch + kv cache warm path. did the autoselect change move a sync prefetch into the hot path?

samir: yes, PR bd91f7e introduced a short-circuit where for certain kernels we call `prefetcher.prefetch_block_sync()` to get better throughput for long-form decoding. it helped throughput in microbenchmarks but added tail latency in mixed workloads.

maya: can we flip that behavior behind the runtime flag? `kernel.autoselect.prefetch_sync=false` as emergency mitigation?

akira: i already tested toggling the flag in a canary host — p99 dropped ~40ms on canary after disabling sync prefetch.

deploy-bot: canary update requested by akira -> rolling out to 3/20 hosts in prod-canary (job 4578). ETA ~4m.

infra-bot: rollout status: 3/20 hosts updated, health checks OK, 0/3 degraded.

maya: awesome. while that rolls, can someone file a revert PR for the sync prefetch chunk? This needs a proper perf/integration test so CI doesn't swallow it next time.

liu: opened draft PR: revert bd91f7e (draft) — link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3921. also bumped the perf job to be non-flaky for streaming workloads.

jamie: for the root cause writeup let's capture two axes: 1) kernel_selector decision moved expensive work into ingress path (sync prefetch) and 2) frame_serializer is doing extra copies when chunk size increased due to larger read windows. both amplify tail latency.

samir: quick mitigation options:
- flip `kernel.autoselect.prefetch_sync=false` (already in flight)
- limit read-ahead window for streaming API via `kernel.max_prefetch_bytes=64KB`
- optimize `frame_serializer::emit_chunks` to avoid an extra memcpy of the block header

maya: also add a CI perf assertion: if streaming p99 regresses >10% on mainline, fail the merge. we need signal gating not flaky noise.

akira: agree. i'll coordinate the revert + patch. jamie can you add a microbenchmark that exercises mixed short+long streaming requests so we don't regress this again?

jamie: on it. will add a harness that simulates 80/20 short/long seq mix and asserts p99 < baseline * 1.08.

liu: after the canary finishes i'll run a rolling rollback test on staging with the revert applied to validate no throughput regression.

deploy-bot: canary update: completed (3/3 batches). observed p99 drop on canary hosts: avg drop 38ms.

infra-bot: prod health checks stable. no new errors.

maya: good job triaging quickly. follow-ups:
- merge revert once benchmark and staging pass
- add CI perf gate for streaming p99
- add telemetry for `kernel.autoselect` decision path (so we can see when prefetch_sync is chosen)
- look into optimizing `frame_serializer::emit_chunks` for zero-copy header/payload emit

akira: I'll create tickets and assign owners. thanks all. :thumbsup:

samir: postmortem note: the microbench targeted throughput improvement but didn't model mixed latency-sensitive streaming traffic. lessons: always include a tail-latency scenario.

maya: leaving this thread open until revert merged + CI gates in place. tagging owners in the tickets.

akira: update: revert merged to staging at 08:10 UTC, staging perf looks good. will schedule prod revert later unless we want to keep the flag off.

jamie: prefer revert + patch for zero-copy, then re-enable autoselect with safe heuristics.

akira: moving to follow-up tickets. closing for now but will reopen if anything else pops.
